title: Unveiling Plasmonic and Photonic Modes in CuS Nanocrystals via Correlative EELS and Cathodoluminescence
content: Copper monosulfide (CuS), particularly in its nanostructured form, exhibits exceptional optoelectronic properties, enabling both plasmonic and photonic absorption [1]. The ability of nanostructured CuS to support localized surface plasmon resonances (LSPRs) in the near-infrared (NIR) spectral range positions it as a compelling candidate for diverse applications [1-5]. This study presents a comprehensive investigation of NIR-to-visible electromagnetic field localization in ultra-thin CuS nanocrystals, achieved through high-resolution electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) in conjunction with cathodoluminescence (CL) spectroscopy. Beyond LSPRs, we also identify a rich spectrum of photonic modes spanning the visible and ultraviolet ranges in colloidally synthesized, single-crystalline CuS nanostructures. Critically, these plasmonic and photonic modes, observed via EELS, are corroborated by rigorous numerical simulations.
